summary: Ephemeral connection hoarding resulting in gradual GPU credit deficit and throttled throughput
description: Issue summary: Since 2026-03-10 09:20 UTC ClearSight's dedicated pool in us-east has experienced a steady decline in p50/p95 throughput for several batched routes. Symptoms include increased GPU credit consumption, progressive failure to attach new workloads, and a rise in allocator 'no free slot' events. Impact: customer-facing latency and retries for synchronous generation endpoints; automatic fallbacks to smaller variants triggered, causing output quality regressions. Environment: Dedicated reserved cluster 'cs-east-1-01' (4xA100), prod-us-east, customer pinned model redwood/rlhf-small-13b, route: /v1/generate (batched).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Route traffic for ClearSight test tenant at 90% of committed throughput (burst pattern every 30s).
2) Observe allocator metrics and GPU credit burn over 30-90 minutes.
3) Trigger synthetic short-lived connections (many small streams) from customer test harness to emulate production pattern.
4) Watch for 'connection_hold' and 'attach_fail' spikes in allocator logs and degraded p50 throughput on per-model dashboards.
logs_and_metrics: 2026-03-10T09:22:17Z allocator: WARN no_free_slot_for_attach tenant=cs-east-01 count=12 backlog=34
2026-03-10T09:24:03Z sidecar: INFO connection_open tenant=cs-east-01 src=10.0.2.45 type=short-stream
GPU credits: baseline for cluster ~ 3.2M tokens/hr; observed drain 4.8M tokens/hr over 45m window
p50 throughput for /v1/generate dropped from 120rps to 68rps over 60 minutes; p95 increased from 1800ms to 4200ms
initial_hypothesis: A leaky connection pattern from customer's SDK or a misbehaving sidecar is holding ephemeral connections open longer than expected, causing allocator to mark slots as reserved and preventing new batched attachments.
The connection hoarding causes gradual GPU credit sink as retries and smaller fallback variants are used more frequently.
Autoscaler cooldowns are preventing rapid replenishment of slots because heartbeats are masked by stale connections.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 10:05 (Aisha): Correlated allocator 'no_free_slot_for_attach' events with a spike in short-lived TCP connections from a single IP range belonging to ClearSight test harness (10.0.2.0/24).
2026-03-10 11:20 (Diego): Captured sidecar traces showing connection state MACHINE->HALF_OPEN for ~45s on average instead of expected <5s for short streams. See trace IDs: trace-ff12ab, trace-ff12ac.
2026-03-10 13:00 (SRE): Confirmed that the dedicated-pool daemon increments slot_reservation for half-open connections; observed reservation leak rate ~0.7 slots/min during peak window.
Checked autoscaler logs: cooldowns prevented new slot allocation for 8 minutes after a burst; metric autoscaler.attach_skips spiked at same intervals.
Memory/driver checks: no GPU OOMs or driver resets in window; NVLink and PCIe metrics nominal. Points to connection/sidecar behavior rather than hardware.
customer_communication: 2026-03-10 10:15 (Support -> ClearSight): Acknowledged impact, requested permission to run targeted synthetic load test and to collect sidecar diagnostics. Customer accepted and provided test harness IP range.
2026-03-10 14:30 (Support): Shared interim findings and suggested short-term mitigation: reduce per-connection keepalive and enable aggressive connection timeouts on customer sidecar (suggested 8s).
2026-03-11 09:00 (Customer): Applied keepalive changes to their SDK in staging and reported initial improvements in connection churn.
temporary_mitigation: 1) Applied a temporary routing rule to limit per-connection concurrency for the ClearSight tenant to 50 concurrent short streams. 2) Increased allocator eviction rate threshold by +10% to free stuck reservations faster during peak bursts. 3) Asked customer to lower sidecar keepalive to 8s as interim measure.
next_steps: 1) Patch runtime to detect and force-close half-open streams older than 10s (dev PR opened).
2) Add allocator metric 'stale_connection_reservations' and alert at >5/min rate.
3) Collaborate with customer to harden SDK connection pooling and roll the change to production traffic window next weekday morning.
4) Re-run capacity forecasting for cluster cs-east-1-01 to validate committed throughput under tightened connection policies.
resolution: Work in progress: temporary mitigation reduced reservation leak rate by ~80% and recovered p50 throughput to ~105rps within 2 hours. A runtime patch to forcibly close half-open short streams is in code review (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1842). Customer agreed to SDK keepalive changes; schedule for production rollout on 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC. Follow-up: create postmortem if issue recurs after rollback period.
